newsitem.title: ITALY: US reaffirms concern over EU grain subsidies.
newsitem.headline: US reaffirms concern over EU grain subsidies.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday reaffirmed its opposition to European Union grain subsidies but said it was still evaluating whether to take any action.

"We continue to be concerned about the resumption of subsidies for export grain...but at this point we have not made a decision to counter this action in part because of our own tight supply of wheat," Lee Schatz, an economist with the grain and feed division of the U.S. Department of Agriculture said.
"We will wait and see how the situation develops," he told Reuters on the sidelines of an international cereals meeting at the U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Organisation in Rome.

The European Union pledged not to undercut U.S. farmers late last year after U.S. grain exporters reacted furiously to its decision to restore the subsidies after a 15-month pause when world prices rose to record levels.

But as bumper crops from southern hemisphere producers like Australia and Argentina begin to hit world markets and prices ease, Brussels is coming under fresh pressure to put its farmers first and pay them subsidies so EU grain cane be sold competitively.
The US-EU deal was designed to stave off yet another damaging and costly transatlantic trade war.
In return for the pledge from Brussels, Washington resisted domestic calls to restore its own subsidies, fearing that would inflate local prices and suck in cheap wheat from Canada.
But US Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman has not ruled out using US subsidies to counter excessive market distortions.
Schatz was attending a meeting of the Intergovernmental Group on Grains, which runs until Friday.
